html:
Tycho Brahe was a Danish nobleman and astronomer who made the most accurate observations of the sky before the telescope.

In 1572 he saw a new star, a supernova, and showed it lay far beyond the Moon, so the heavens could change after all. The king gave him the island of Hven in the Sound, now Swedish, where he built the observatory of Uraniborg. For twenty years he and his assistants measured the planets and stars with great instruments of his own design.

He fell out with a new king and moved to Prague in 1599, where he died. His assistant Johannes Kepler used his records of Mars to find that planets move in ellipses, a key step of the Scientific Revolution after Copernicus. Tycho is a hero of Danish science.
